knowledge_type_note: Official rule. Underpromotion is a consequence of the rule, not a separate rule.
definition_short: A pawn reaching the far rank is replaced, as part of the same move, by a queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour.
definition_long:
A pawn reaching the eighth rank (first rank for Black) must be exchanged, as part of the same move, for a new queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour. The choice is not restricted to pieces already captured, and there is no limit on how many of a kind may be on the board.

FIDE Art. 4.6 governs the physical act: 'the pawn does not have to be placed on the square of arrival', the order of removing pawn and placing piece does not matter, and 'if an opponent's piece stands on the square of promotion, it must be captured.' Art. 4.4.4: the choice is finalised when the new piece touches the promotion square.

Choosing something other than a queen is UNDERPROMOTION, and is correct when a queen would stalemate, or when a knight's move is what the position needs (a check or fork a queen cannot give).

preconditions: A pawn is moving to the eighth rank (White) or first rank (Black)

exceptions: Promotion is compulsory: a pawn may not remain a pawn.
Underpromotion to a rook avoids stalemate where a queen would cause it; underpromotion to a knight gains a check or fork unavailable to a queen.
limitations: TYPICAL_CONFIDENCE RAISED medium -> high, 2026-09-02, and the reason is the schema's own definition of the field: 'how confidently this concept can normally be asserted ONCE ITS PRECONDITIONS HOLD'. This concept's recognition is MECHANICAL and its knowledge type already carries a high ceiling, so once the preconditions hold there is nothing left to be uncertain about - a stalemate is a stalemate, and a fork this base reports is one findMotifs() found, which ARCHITECTURE.md makes the authority and forbids second-guessing. 'Medium' was the default across 32 rule and motif records regardless of detectability, and it was found by measuring what the API reports against what each record permits: twelve concepts were reporting ABOVE their own record. The fix was to make each record its own ceiling in cap(), which then required the records that were wrong to be corrected rather than silently overruled.

examples.note: a pawn can promote on this move (f8=Q+). This is a DEFINITIONAL example: the feature is present by the rules of chess and by the page's own move generator, which is the whole of what needs verifying. No engine was consulted, because no engine is needed to establish that a legal move exists. Provenance: the puzzle corpus is engine self-play — a real position from a real game between engines, not a master game.

counterexamples.note: A white pawn on the seventh rank and it can never promote. The enemy king stands on the queening square, nothing sits on d8 or f8 to capture, and no white piece can drive the king away - so the pawn is one square from the eighth rank for ever. The rule is not in doubt here and its PRECONDITION is: promotion happens when a pawn REACHES the far rank, and reaching it is a separate question the rule says nothing about. This base's positive example is the rule; this is the condition under it.

by_level.beginner: A pawn reaching the far end of the board turns into another piece — almost always a queen.
by_level.intermediate: Promotion. A queen is right nearly always, but check for stalemate, and check whether a knight would give a decisive check or fork.
by_level.advanced: Art. 3.7.5 / 4.6. Underpromotion is justified by stalemate avoidance or by knight geometry.

by_depth.short: A pawn reaching the far rank becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight of its own colour.
by_depth.normal: Promotion: a pawn arriving on the eighth rank is replaced immediately, as part of the same move, by a piece of its own colour. The choice is free and unlimited — a side may have several queens — and it is not confined to pieces already captured.
by_depth.deep: FIDE Art. 3.7.5 with Art. 4.6 on completing the move. Underpromotion has exactly two standard justifications and both are geometric rather than material: a rook instead of a queen because the queen would stalemate, and a knight because the knight reaches squares no queen does, most often with check. Everything else is a queen. The rule is also what makes a passed pawn worth calculating rather than counting.

audit_notes: 2026-09-01: detector field named 'promotionAvailable', which does not exist anywhere in the codebase. The audit's hardcoded whitelist had been accepting it. Repointed at real code, or marked as proposed where nothing implements it.

validation_na.false_positive_test: N/A rather than missing. A registered false-positive case is a position where the concept's surface pattern is present and the concept is absent, replayed as an assertion so the system can be shown declining the error. This concept is DECIDED BY THE MOVE GENERATOR - the same function that decides it in a game - so there is no judgement to get wrong and no surface pattern that can be present without the thing itself. The nearest genuine risk is a PATTERN NAME attached to a position that is check and not mate, and that risk belongs to `back-rank-mate` and `smothered-mate`, both of which carry a registered case for it.
